title: 6 people injured after vehicle strikes pedestrians in Saint-Tite, Que.
summary: The incident happened on Saint-Joseph Boulevard as the town is hosting the Festival Western de Saint-Tite, a major attraction for the region.

image.caption: Several people are injured in St-Tite, Que. (Martin Labbé/Radio-Canada)

blocks.text: The incident happened on Saint-Joseph Boulevard as the town is hosting the Festival Western de Saint-Tite, a major attraction for the region.
Quebec provincial police are investigating after six people were injured after they were struck by a vehicle in Saint-Tite, Que., early Saturday morning.
Police say a collision between a vehicle and pedestrians took place on Saint-Joseph Boulevard. Witnesses say police arrived on scene around 4:30 a.m.
The vehicle fled the scene, according to the Sûreté du Québec. It was later found in the Quebec City region around 5:30 a.m.
A man in his 20s was arrested by police and is being questioned by investigators.
The victims were transported to hospital with various injuries, the extent of which are unknown at this time.

items: After 20 years with no police force, safety tops voter concerns in this Quebec community

blocks.text: The town is hosting the popular Festival Western de St-Tite and three Quebec political leaders are expected on site today as part of their respective campaigns.
Festival officials say Saturday's activities will go ahead as planned.

"An isolated incident beyond our control occurred early this morning on Saint-Joseph Boulevard. Our thoughts are with those involved and their families. We wish them a speedy recovery," the organizers said in a statement.

"The safety of our festival-goers, volunteers, and staff remains our top priority. The Festival is a festive event where everyone should feel safe. That's why every effort is being made to ensure this."
Police say Saint-Joseph Boulevard will remain closed to vehicle traffic between Du Couvent and Moulin Streets for most of Saturday as investigators and technicians work on the scene.

The early morning incident took place as three Quebec party leaders were expected to attend the festival. The Quebec Liberals (PLQ), Coalition Avenir Québec (CAQ) and the Parti Québécois (PQ) all had stops planned for Saturday.
CAQ Leader Christine Fréchette posted her condolences to the victims on X.

“My thoughts are with the victims, their loved ones, and all those affected by the events that took place at the Western Festival in St-Tite. The ongoing investigation will determine the causes of this act,” Fréchette said.
PQ Leader Pierre St-Pierre Plamondon also offered his condolences.

“My thoughts are with the injured individuals, their loved ones, and all those who witnessed the distressing scene in Saint-Tite.,” St-Pierre Plamondon wrote on X. "Thank you to the first responders who acted quickly. Quebecers should be able to enjoy places where they can gather and celebrate safely."
